liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The first-set close features a very spacey coda for a robust opening act; Garcia's third solo run is described as interesting but a bit tentative and lost [10][11]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): The band is clearly on from the first note, making the show smooth and solid [10]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Donna's harmonies with Bobby and Jerry are praised in this performance [13]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): The performance crackles with electricity, standing out as a highlight of the concert [6]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): The reviewer considers this the best version they have heard of the song [7]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-17.121485.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 215 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd77-05-17.sbd.weiner.18554.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 194 min; rated 4.68/5 by 79 [3]. Said about its sound: Songs feature a funky back-beat, possibly influenced by Marley's Exodus release that month [13]
- **gd1977-05-17.sbd.leonard.1107.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4.58/5 by 12 [4]
- **gd1977-05-17.sbd.stretch.5420.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [5]

## Around the show

- The reviewer is an Auburn student and fan, making Tuscaloosa a difficult location to enjoy [14]
- The reviewer attended the show in Tuscaloosa and knows older heads who were there [16]
- The transition into Fire On The Mountain ranks among the best ever recorded [6]
- The performance is not yet on par with many other Spring 1977 shows [11]
- Rivals but does not overcome the greatness of the May 8, 1977 show [14]
- The two-week run rivals Europe 1972, though lacking the crazy Dark Stars of then [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-17.121485.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by matrix by dusborne; source: 2 source matrix: Soundboard (shnid=18554): SBDMR > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN and Aud (shnid=88771): Recording by Steve Maizner: Sony ECM-990s>Sony TC153; Transfer… [1]. Also: Thanks Noah Weiner for SBD work, Steve Maizner for recording, David Minches for AUD transfer [1]
- **gd77-05-17.sbd.weiner.18554.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [3]. Also: Released on a two-CD set by Phil in the late 1990s with great bass licks [7]
- **gd1977-05-17.sbd.leonard.1107.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Brian Leopard; source: SBD>MR 7" (Baked)>DAT>Cass>DAT>CD [4]. Also: Received on disc and EAC'd by the uploader; tuning pauses shortened in some cases [4]
- **gd1977-05-17.sbd.stretch.5420.shnf**: source: S:Rm (7" - baked), D, C, D - 1x90Meter (and Potentially 2x60Meter?) [5]. Also: Setlist includes Minglewood Blues through Sugar Magnolia, with specific transitions noted [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Patrick D. Covert: [Grateful Dead Tuscaloosa AL 1977 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1295788/Grateful-Dead-Tuscaloosa-AL-1977-Concert-Poster) [19]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 5/17/77 Memorial Coliseum - Uni…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27304785971/) [20]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27304785971/) [21]
